title: ExoNotes: do ExoFOP observer notes carry disposition signal beyond the numeric TOI catalogue?
description: Do the free-text observing notes astronomers write on TESS Objects of Interest carry disposition-relevant information that the numeric catalogue columns do not? A pre-registered study. Free text is converted to numeric semantic features with a System One model (Jev, TypeSafe AI) used strictly as a featurizer ; gradient boosting is the predictor and cross-validation grouped by host star is the arbiter. Model probabilities are never thresholded into a decision. Result. All six pre-registered gates pass, including stability under paraphrase, a temporal split, a leakage-stripped arm and a missingness ablation. Why it is not a leakage signature. The gain survives a metadata control capturing note count, note length and author identity (+0.0220, CI +0.0126 to +0.0321), so it is not merely a record of which follow-up group wrote a note. title: Jev in Practice: A Composable Python Toolkit for TypeSafe's System One Decision Model
description: Jev is TypeSafe's flagship System One decision model: instead of generating text, it answers typed questions (Choice, Score, Noul) about a state with calibrated probabilities that software can branch on directly. This work presents daf-jev , an open, modular, composable Python toolkit for the Jev API, together with a live-API characterization of the model. The package layers ergonomic question builders, a decision-composition library (confidence gates, tiered routing, composite scoring), a concurrent corpus evaluator, a calibration module, a CLI, an agent skill, and a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server over a thin typed client. Live benchmarks show that batching questions into one call is faster and cheaper than sequential calls (up to ~18x speedup and ~4x fewer tokens), that decision pipelines complete within the model's millisecond envelope, and that reported confidence is self-consistent across repeated evaluations. All numbers in the accompanying manuscript are generated from benchmark artifacts; the full provenance chain (hashed documentation snapshot, figure registry, validation receipts) is machine-checked.

title: Plan Once, Ground Locally: Plan-and-Execute Web Agents Match ReAct Accuracy at One-Sixth of the Token Cost
description: LLM web agents usually follow the ReAct pattern: the model is called again after every browser action, so each click is paid for with a network round trip and with a prompt that has grown since the last one. We study the alternative in which the model writes the whole plan in one call and the steps are executed locally, with a small on-device decision model (Laya, a ModernBERT-large "System-1" model used zero-shot) mapping each step to a page element, judging when asynchronous content has arrived, and checking actions that left the page unchanged. We evaluate on a new benchmark of 200 tasks across seven public websites whose ground truth is scraped from the sites themselves or produced by scripted browser runs, and graded by fixed regular expressions. Every task was run three times under four configurations with the same LLM (DeepSeek v4.1 flash): ReAct, ReAct with a reading and turn budget matched to the plan agent, plan-and-execute with Laya, and an ablation that replaces Laya with word-overlap matching, for 2,400 runs, plus 400 further runs with a second model. Against the budget-matched baseline, planning once is not significantly different on success (88.8% vs 92.0%; paired difference -3.2 points, 95% CI -7.7 to +1.2) while using 83.6% fewer input tokens, 67.3% fewer LLM calls and 80.4% less money, and finishing 4.1x faster. title: Audio-Laya: direct speech-to-decision classification with a frozen Whisper encoder and a trainable projector
description: Research prototype that classifies call audio as legitimate or spam directly from audio, without an intermediate transcription step. title: wev: Distilling LLM Browser Agents into Open, Local System-One Decision Models
description: System-One decision models answer typed questions about a free-form state with a probability for every declared option, in one forward pass and without generating text, but the open models of this kind are trained on general decision data and reach at most 21% step success on browser steps from unseen websites. We observe that the typed interface between a browser agent and its System One is itself a source of supervision: a prompted LLM placed behind it while the agent works on live websites produces training data in exactly the decision model's format, and an LLM judge reading each episode's final page decides which episodes to keep. We combine this interface distillation with Mind2Web and NNetNav demonstrations converted to the same format, after auditing NNetNav's stopping labels, and with general decision corpora. The resulting open models, wev-1.7b, wev-4b and wev-8b, build on Qwen3 base models. wev-4b answers 76% of browser steps on unseen websites correctly and stays competitive on general decision benchmarks. As the System One of an open browser agent, it completes as many held-out live-website tasks as its LLM teacher, at 15-320 ms per decision on one consumer GPU. Jun Huang and Xin Ren contributed equally. Code, models and data: https://github.com/alanhuangyoo/wev

title: Preregistration: A bias-corrected, entropy-stratified test of whether TypeSafe AI's Jev lowers its confidence when humans disagree (ChaosNLI)
description: Preregistration for an independent study of TypeSafe AI's Jev decision model (jev-1.13.0). Independent study. Not affiliated with or endorsed by TypeSafe AI. title: Jev in Medicine: A Benchmark Evaluation
description: Background : Jev is a non-generative System One model that assigns probabilities to predefined answer options and cannot answer outside them. Its calibration and its performance on complex diagnostic cases remain insufficiently characterised. Methods : We evaluated Jev 1.13 on four medical benchmarks: MetaMedQA (1,373 examination questions), PubMedQA (500 research questions), DiagnosisArena-MCQ (915 cases) and the NEJM Case Challenges (34 cases). GPT-6 Sol, with and without reasoning, was the reference. Outcomes were top-1 accuracy (primary), calibration, selective prediction and recognition of unanswerable questions Results : Jev's accuracy was similar to that of GPT-6 Sol with medium reasoning on PubMedQA (78.4% vs 78.2%), lower on MetaMedQA (74.8% vs 82.7%) and much lower on DiagnosisArena-MCQ (59.8% vs 82.4%) and the NEJM cases (61.8% vs 82.4%, adjusted P = 0.078). title: Semantic Relativity Theory v3.3P
description: Semantic Relativity Theory v3.3P extends the observer-conditional framework of TRS v3.2P into structured AI classification systems whose outputs can activate operational branches. The paper distinguishes schema conformance from execution repeatability, reformulation invariance, material-change sensitivity, and observer-conditioned operational risk. Its empirical grounding comprises 41 controlled texts and 287 cleaned observations across three tested AI configurations. The results show that schema-valid outputs can coexist with decision changes under equivalent reformulation, repeated execution, and cross-system comparison. The publication reports the conceptual extension, aggregate empirical results, limitations, and experimental-governance requirements. Operational formulas, weights, thresholds, calibration procedures, protected corpora, scripts, case-level outputs, and decision boundaries remain outside the public disclosure boundary.

title: When Does Selection Replace Extraction? A Pre-Registered Test of Agent Memory with a Typed Decision Model
description: Does conversational memory need LLM-extracted facts, or is selecting the right raw turns enough? Published results disagree. Extraction-based systems report gains from distilled facts. Recent studies find raw history with good ranking does as well, but disagree about whether ranking matters. We ran a pre-registered study on held-out LoCoMo conversations and LongMemEval. At a tight budget on LoCoMo, raw turns selected by a single call to Jev, a typed decision model, are non-inferior to an LLM-extraction memory (one-sided 95% bound −3.0 points against a −5-point margin). Blind human grading narrows the margin but does not change the result. Raw turns cost 3,061× less to write, and the result holds with a second answer model. Within this study, reranking's gain shrinks as the budget grows. It adds 17.4 points on LoCoMo and 9.1 on LongMemEval when three of 30 candidates are kept. At generous budgets it adds 1.5 and 1.1, and extraction systems are more accurate. This suggests why published results disagree. At matched context, Jev selects as accurately as an LLM reranker (non-inferiority bound −2.0) at a third of the latency, and more accurately than a multi-call graph traversal. Reranking lowers correct abstention. Plans, code and graded answers are released. title: Reflex-1: frontier-LLM accuracy at Jev speed with a 4B open model
description: Reflex-1 is a 4B open decision model built on Google Gemma 4 E4B for routing, guardrails and classification. It returns a choice with probabilities instead of generated text. In instant mode it reads option probabilities in a single forward pass and matches the accuracy band of frontier LLMs (GPT-5.6, Gemini 3.8) and the dedicated judgment API Jev on five public classification benchmarks, at 0.10 s median latency on one GPU; it also classifies images. In deep mode, trained per judgment, it solves decisions that require reasoning through latent reasoning, with each latent step supervised through the model's shared LM head so that it can be decoded back into words, reaching frontier-level accuracy at about one second per question on trained tasks.

title: Evaluating and Benchmarking the System One Model Jev
Schema Conformance Does Not Guarantee Decision Stability: When the Decision Is Typed but the Interpretation Isn't
description: Structured outputs constrain an AI system to return a valid category, schema, and numeric scores that downstream software can process, but schema adherence is not the same property as decision stability. This paper reports a controlled supplier-payment classification pilot across three frontier model configurations, using 41 texts and 287 cleaned observations. The corpus comprises one base case, 20 meaning-preserving reformulations, and 20 loaded perturbations. The results distinguish structural validity from reformulation invariance, execution repeatability, and sensitivity to material changes. One tested configuration changed its majority decision on 5 of 20 equivalent reformulations; the three configurations disagreed on 12 of 41 texts; and repeated identical inputs produced a 21.1% pairwise decision-discordance rate in one configuration. The study is a single-domain pilot and does not establish provider-only causal effects, probabilistic calibration, or universal properties of structured-output systems. It concludes that schema conformance and decision stability should be evaluated separately and complemented by deterministic validation and authoritative reference retrieval where operational decisions depend on external facts.

title: GUYASOILeDNA: a trans-kingdom and functional eDNA dataset on soil biodiversity from diverse land-cover types in French Guiana
description: Soil biodiversity represents approximately 60% of all described species on Earth and plays a critical role in terrestrial ecosystem functioning. However, knowledge of tropical soil biota and their roles remains highly fragmentary, especially in hyperdiverse tropical regions that remain largely undersampled relative to their temperate counterparts. Recent non-invasive methods, such as environmental DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding, have enabled large-scale data collection across kingdoms of life and habitats, including understudied compartments such as soils. Here, GUYASOILeDNA is presented as the first large-scale eDNA metabarcoding dataset of tropical soil Bacteria (16S), Eukaryota (18S), Fungi (ITS1), and Insecta (16S) from French Guiana. This dataset describes the distribution of 69,881 operational taxonomic units (OTUs) in 1,410 soil samples collected across a variety of forest types, savannas, pastures, and urban areas. In addition, functional annotations based on trophic guild assignments are provided for 51% of the OTUs. This dataset can be used for meta-analyses, exploring soil taxonomic and functional diversity in relation to environmental factors, studying spatial associations among soil groups, and informing protected area management, among other applications. While this dataset represents an important first step toward understanding soil biodiversity in the region, it also reveals key gaps that may guide future research.

title: Epistemic Calibration and Latency Advantages of System One Probabilistic Agents in Limit Order Book Microstructure: An Empirical and Multi-Agent Evaluation
description: Autoregressive Large Language Models (LLMs) operating under the deliberative System Two paradigm encounter severe structural bottlenecks when deployed in electronic financial markets: token-by-token sequential decoding induces unacceptable execution latencies (3,500-12,000 ms), unstructured text outputs trigger syntactic parsing failures, and coarse sentiment classifiers fail to identify semantic camouflage in corporate disclosures . This paper formulates, deploys, and empirically evaluates a System One probabilistic decision agent powered by TypeSafe AI's foundation model (jev-1.13.0) and optimized via Reinforcement Learning from Classifier Decisions (RLCD) . By restricting the action space to a strictly typed simplex A4 = {HOLD, LONG, SHORT, CLOSE} evaluated in a single forward pass O(1), the agent achieves sub-second inference (mean latency 241.18 ms, compliance 98.8% < 500 ms) and rigorous epistemic calibration (ECE = 0.0228, Brier Score = 0.0274) . On empirical Level 2 (L2) tick data from Binance Futures (BTCUSDT), the bidirectional agent delivers +739.70 bps net of friction with a Sharpe ratio of 14.92, identifying the critical latency extinction threshold at 1,485.00 ms .

title: Decision Theory and Artificial Intelligence
description: Artificial intelligence supports a decision only through a feasible action and its reward. We develop a common framework linking action spaces, reward functions, statistical estimation, and costly information acquisition. We characterize minimal output contracts for specified reward families, decompose decision regret, and connect regression error to routing regret under capacity constraints. An acquisition-output contract characterizes which compressed representations preserve every nonnegative-price routing decision and bounds the loss when they do not. A routing-geometry dichotomy distinguishes discrete decisions, where information can be most valuable near an action boundary, from continuous quadratic sizing, where precision gains can favor the strongest signals. Delay, position limits, and conditional refinement determine when these patterns change. The framework accommodates supervised learning (SL), unsupervised learning (UL), reinforcement learning (RL), large language models (LLMs), and typed decision models such as JEV. SL estimates outcome statistics or action values; UL constructs representations whose usefulness depends on the reward-relevant information they preserve; RL learns policies or action values for sequential rewards. LLMs generate candidate answers or judgments, while JEV supplies probabilities over specified categories, propositions, or rubric levels. title: Institution-Specific Local AI for Network Defense: An Early Exploration of Intrusion Detection and Graduated Response with a Local Decision Model and Retrieval-Augmented Decision-Making (RAD)
description: In the hands of attackers, AI is rapidly widening both the attack surface and the range of attack techniques. Meanwhile, most organisations still defend themselves with static rules or with cloud-based services that require sending their data outside. This paper explores a different path: a small local decision model (Laya, 421M parameters) that runs on a single consumer laptop without any cloud connection. We use it to detect network intrusions and connect those detections safely to a graduated response. We study the model in a two-factor (2×2) design, fine-tuning × retrieval-augmented decision-making (RAD), and compare it with rule-based and anomaly-based baselines. The evaluation has two parts: reproducible synthetic IDS logs (20 replications, 3 training seeds) and an independent real network-traffic capture (CIC-IDS2017, PCAP → Zeek). On the synthetic test set, the fine-tuned model with RAD reaches F1 0.89, versus 0.66 for the rule-based baseline. On an attack never seen in training, the rule and anomaly baselines detect nothing, while the model detects 0.92 of attack windows. On the real traffic capture, without any retraining, it detects SSH brute-force attacks with F1 0.98–0.99 and no false alarms, outperforming the rule-based baseline. It does not generalise to slow port scans that differ in form from those seen in training. The whole system runs without sharing data and without paying an external provider. title: Confidence-gated reranking with Jev raises domain-name segmentation accuracy
description: In domain-name segmentation, every way of putting the spaces back is a possible split; the task is to pick the most plausible one. This report (13 slides) shows confidence-gated reranking with Jev: dksplit 1.0.2 narrows each name to its three most likely readings, Jev 1.13.0 (TypeSafe AI) reranks them and gives a probability for each, and Jev's choice is kept when that probability is high enough. title: Yway: A Burmese System One Decision Model
description: We present Yway (ရွေး, "choose"), a small decision model for Burmese (Myanmar) text. Instead of generating text, Yway answers typed questions (pick an option, yes/no, or a level) with calibrated probabilities, following the "System One" design of TypeSafe's Jev and the open Laya model. It reuses Laya's decision head and its reinforcement-learning objective with proper scoring rules, but replaces Laya's multilingual encoder with XLM RoBERTa-base, which tokenizes Burmese 2.3× more efficiently. title: Paraphrastic Resistance: Text Fragility Is Not Decision Instability
description: Typed AI systems can return schema-valid and exactly repeatable outputs while changing their decisions under controlled variations in wording, checkpoint, or class semantics. This study asks whether such configuration sensitivity can be explained by fragility in the source texts. Two experiments crossed the Index of Paraphrastic Resistance (IRP) with a frozen 41-text corpus and a 2 × 2 Laya design comprising two checkpoints and two class-semantics treatments. In Experiment A, neutral IRP was nearly unrelated to the number of distinct decisions across the four cells, r = −.081. The 38 texts that changed category had a mean IRP of 8.06; the three stable texts had a mean of 8.34. Checkpoint replacement produced the largest exact-category shift, while added class definitions produced smaller, checkpoint-dependent changes. In Experiment B, two Gemini-family evaluators scored the same texts with defined and minimal class context. The mean defined-minus-minimal shift was −0.14 for Evaluator 1 and −0.56 for Evaluator 2; cross-evaluator ordering remained moderately similar, r ≈ .67 to .68. The evidence separates semantic robustness of the input from stability of the decision boundary. Neither property can be inferred from schema conformance, exact repetition, or the other property alone.

description: This paper reports a direct ground-truth comparison between a standalone Index of Paraphrastic Resistance gate and a typed decision supervisor in a controlled three-node invoicing chain. Thirty synthetic customer records passed through three transmission modalities, producing 90 condition-level trajectories. description: This preprint evaluates Jev, a typed per-turn supervisor for software-engineering agents. Each comparison uses a different complete-pair task set. The experiment does not establish an improvement from active supervision or demonstrate that its effect is zero. description: Know-your-business onboarding requires deciding who may legally bind a company.
